event.detail:
# Uninstall can leave a previously orphaned private tmux server

Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d

## TLDR

A legacy private tmux server that already outlived a stopped supervisor can keep running after remote uninstall, including after removal of the host entry and its installed binary.

## Details

backend.rs:3303-3345 stops a service unless inactive/failed, then confirms and cleans terminal hosts, without the former private-socket lookup or tmux kill-server. SPEC.md:214-217 says exactly: 'Uninstall has no tmux step of its own: stopping the supervisor's service ends whatever still runs under it, an earlier release's private tmux server included, but one that outlived a supervisor stopped before uninstall (on a host never updated to a release that ends it at startup, say) keeps running, which the maintainer accepted on 2026-11-11.' Only source line wrapping removed. SPEC_impl.md:7853-7863 includes the same residual after failed startup ending followed by later supervisor stop.

Synthesis scope clarification: this proposed acceptance applies only to the already stopped/orphaned private-server residual on uninstall. It says nothing about permission to mutate an answering old supervisor during Add. Direct source checks for that separate premise are in c4: Add discovery and confirmation adopt answering supervisors, including protocol-skewed peers, and finish_use_as_is skips planned steps without executing cleanup. The accepted residual also does not excuse failed terminal-host termination; backend.rs:3309-3339 still fails those checks before later lib removal. Caller-supplied g048/c1, g047/c1 and g046/f1 identify the same orphan-server boundary; g047/c3 concerns fixture evidence and is not evidence that active-unit or terminal-host cleanup actually ran.

Suggested bucket: other for the established residual-process cleanup consequence, preserving original possible highest for independent determination; no lowering or drop has been accepted by the parent. Could-be-highest: yes, original concern involved user-owned processes left unmanaged; no separate source route to loss of work or security impact has been established. Confidence: confirmed source/contract conclusion, no execution. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance above, proposed only for the already orphaned server residual. possible_cover: cited contracts and caller-supplied related group records only; excluded queue coverage not read. Material caveats: active control-group termination remains a specified implementation contract, not observed behavior; ordinary Add adoption, update replacement and terminal-host cleanup retain distinct obligations. No missing premise remains for the stated residual and its exact acceptance.

event.summary: GNU-stat file removal is confined to Linux plans and preserves errors
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d. TLDR: considered whether the new cleanup uses incompatible tools on remote Macs, silently skips inaccessible files, or follows a bundled-tmux symlink into another file. Details: backend.rs:3393-3397 uses GNU stat syntax but plan.rs:811-839 returns the Mac action list before Linux RemoveBundledTmux is appended at :867-869; service.rs:2778-2785 is the sole production caller. stat without -L inspects the link itself, and rm -f unlinks the named file without following its final symlink. backend.rs:34-36 only accepts C-locale missing-path diagnostics; other lookup errors explicitly exit nonzero. A successful stat followed by a refused rm leaves rm as the branch status, so require_shell reports failure, converted by service.rs:2781 to a warning. Local unlink at :3373-3379 similarly skips only NotFound. SPEC.md:182-188 requires an absent-file skip and warning on failed removal; :193-194 excludes Mac tmux actions. Suggested bucket: other for tooling portability/diagnostics; could-be-highest: false for these refuted routes, since symlink targets are not followed by the deletion. Confidence: confirmed source analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutes these concerns. possible_cover: none.

event.summary: Linux cleanup preserves lookup errors and unlinks only the final entry
event.detail:
# Cleanup's portability and final-entry behavior have narrow guarantees

Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d

## TLDR

The original concerns were incompatible cleanup tools on remote Macs, inaccessible files silently treated as absent, and following the bundled-tmux file's own symbolic link to delete its target. These specific routes are refuted by source.

## Details

backend.rs:3393-3397 uses GNU stat syntax, but plan.rs:811-839 returns the Mac action list before :867-869 appends Linux RemoveBundledTmux; service.rs:2778-2785 dispatches that action. stat without -L describes the final symbolic link itself, and rm -f unlinks that entry rather than its target. The local remove_file at :3373-3379 has the same final-entry behavior. This is not a claim that intermediate path components cannot be symbolic links or change concurrently. backend.rs:34-36 accepts only C-locale missing-path diagnostics; all other lookup failures explicitly exit nonzero. A refused rm remains the shell branch's failing exit status, which require_shell reports and service.rs:2781 converts to a warning. SPEC.md:182-188 requires absent-file skip and warning on failure, and :193-194 excludes tmux operations on remote Macs.

Suggested bucket: other for the original portability/diagnostic concerns. Could-be-highest: false for these specific refuted routes; no security or loss-of-work route was established. Confidence: confirmed source analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation limited to Mac plan reachability, positive absence/error propagation and unlinking the final symbolic link itself. Parent has accepted no proposed drop. possible_cover: none. Caveat: c4 separately covers the fixed private path and Add admission; this record does not establish global filesystem-race safety or justify deleting a user's shared-bin copy.

event.summary: Add adopts an answering old supervisor before cleanup can execute
event.detail:
# Add admission prevents cleanup beneath an answering supervisor

Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d

## TLDR

The original concern was that Add could remove bundled tmux while an older running supervisor still needed it, breaking terminal operations and potentially affecting work. The other original concern was deleting the user's executable beside a supervisor installed in a shared folder.

## Details

Direct source checks this synthesis turn resolve the ordinary answering-supervisor route. service.rs:835-900 registers both compatible and protocol-skewed answering supervisors without constructing an Add installation plan; only Absent reaches planning at :901-932. Confirmation re-probes the original coordinates at :2238 and, when distinct, planned install coordinates at :2239-2249. Both answering outcomes return UseAsIs (:2251-2309); only Absent returns Execute (:2311). revalidate_and_execute dispatches UseAsIs to finish_use_as_is, separately from execute (:2215-2220). backend.rs:2648-2652 requires the positive-absence exit code, empty stdout and remote command-start evidence; a timeout/malformed hello fails rather than becoming absence (:2670-2681). SPEC.md:103-106 states: 'If one is already running — say one the user started interactively by hand — the helm uses it as-is; it never restarts or replaces a running supervisor.'

## TLDR

The original concern was that Add could remove bundled tmux while an older running supervisor still needed it, breaking terminal operations and potentially affecting work. The other original concern was deleting the user's executable beside a supervisor installed in a shared folder.

## Details

Confirmation re-probes the original coordinates at :2238 and, when distinct, planned install coordinates at :2239-2249. SPEC.md:103-106 states: 'If one is already running — say one the user started interactively by hand — the helm uses it as-is; it never restarts or replaces a running supervisor.'

This corrects the earlier phase-order-only rationale: systemctl enable --now success alone does not prove replacing a pre-existing process. Add's admission/adoption gates supply the missing premise. Update separately plans RestartSupervisor before removal; sequential action execution stops on restart error. Fixed-path conclusions remain narrow: plan.rs:722-725,737-740,867-869 freezes the private lib path independently of a shared binary destination, so it does not remove the shared-bin tmux. backend.rs:3373-3408 unlinks the final symlink itself and preserves lookup/removal failures; that does not assert safety against all intermediate-parent path changes.

Suggested bucket: high for the original hypothetical broken terminal operations; retain possible highest for affected work, with no work-loss route established. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of ordinary Add over an already-answering old supervisor at the probed installation; no runtime behavior observed. proposed_drop: source refutation through discovery, confirmation and distinct UseAsIs dispatch, plus the separately scoped fixed-path conclusion. Parent has accepted no drop. possible_cover: caller-supplied g048/l1 and g046/c3 concern the same Add route; no excluded queue coverage read. Caveats: a concurrent external start after confirmation is a different race, not established here. l1's accepted orphan-private-server uninstall residual does not authorize disruption of an answering supervisor and is not the basis for this proposed drop. The c4 lead is resolved under this ID; earlier events remain preserved.

Additional source check: service.rs:2546-2559 confirms finish_use_as_is only marks the run completed and planned steps skipped, clears busy, and publishes events; it does not invoke installation or cleanup. backend.rs:1602-1617 confirms the remote probe searches PATH and the two standard private-lib/shared-bin locations before reporting missing executable, and execs the selected binary with the frozen state argument. These checks settle the remaining adoption-completion and ordinary fallback-location premises. No new consequence or open lead arose.
